core_obligations: Direct sums (proof lines 2238-2253): for a family of objects the author shows that the termwise direct sum of arbitrary representatives is a direct sum in the derived category, by checking the universal property against the description of morphisms in the derived category.

Products (proof lines 2254-2259): choosing a K-injective resolution of each object, the author claims that the termwise product of the resolutions is a product in the derived category and attributes this to the cited result on products of K-injective complexes; both assertions together give that the derived category has direct sums and products.
proof_roadmap: Show that termwise direct sums compute direct sums in the derived category.
Resolve each object K-injectively and take the termwise product.
Cite the product rule for K-injective complexes to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category has direct sums and products, computed termwise, products being computed on K-injective representatives (statement lines 2225-2236). The proof is a complete argument: the direct sum statement is verified against the description of morphisms in the derived category (proof lines 2238-2253), and the product statement is reduced to the product rule for K-injective complexes by resolving each object K-injectively (proof lines 2254-2259). The non-formal content is the verification of the two universal properties. The claim is H2.
